operation: At the current parse-that UTF-16 offset, consume one maximal CSS Syntax 3 number prefix and return its semantic number leaf.
guards: A dot belongs to the number only when followed by an ASCII digit.
An exponent marker belongs to the number only when followed by an ASCII digit or by a sign and an ASCII digit.
The parser succeeds on the maximal valid prefix and leaves all following source to its parent production.

result.shape: Readonly<{ value: number; type: 'integer' | 'number'; sign: '+' | '-' | null }>
result.value: JavaScript binary64 Number of the exact consumed representation, preserving Object.is(-0).
result.type: integer exactly when the consumed representation contains neither a decimal point nor an exponent marker.
result.sign: The explicit leading sign or null.

failure: No throw; one parse-that failure at the entry offset; the ParserState source, predecessor value, offset, and pre-existing-ahead diagnostics remain transactional.

implementation_law.required: One readable exported @mkbabb/parse-that@1.0.0 parser assembled directly from public combinators.
implementation_law.note: A parse-that regex terminal is an idiomatic combinator leaf, not a forbidden external regex parser. There is no combinator-call quota or required construction shape.

candidate_law.isolation: Each author receives this exact contract, the common public harness, and only that seat's lineage packet and named lineage sources.
candidate_law.selection: After all four payloads close and the fresh holdout is revealed, five independent skeptics review the same exact candidate set; three further disjoint adjudicators may select only one already reviewed unblocked exact hash.

benchmark_law: Benchmark qualification occurs after candidate closure and correctness, not in pre-author admission. It must execute exact source/build/bundle/corpus/runner/schedule bytes, retain at least two attempts, compare identical work and observations, compute its own statistics, and require strict wins over comparable live-regex, deposed, and C14 peers without correctness relaxation.
